_about: A319-100 with sharklets, from Airbus AC A319 (Jul 01/26) 2-2-0 Sharklet sheets 3 (side, front: page index 43) and 4 (plan: page index 44). Pixels of layers.py --mode strokes-in-fill rasters at scale 20, line centres; the side and plan with --xscale 1.0249 (both sheets are drawn 2.5% short lengthwise against their printed 33.84 m and 11.04 m; their heights and widths match the A320's sheets). The A320's points moved onto these sheets (a319/*.anchors.json says how) and snapped. Of the two overwing exits drawn, the first is marked optional: the shape has the standard one. The cockpit panes are the A320's (the same nose), which land on this sheet's. Windows the drawing hides (behind the sharklet's and wing's lines, a dimension line, and in the optional exit) are placed at the drawing's pitch (windowsAlso).

sources.title: Airbus, A319 Aircraft Characteristics: Airport and Maintenance Planning (Jul 01/26), 2-2-0 General Aircraft Dimensions, Sharklet sheets 3 and 4
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the side, plan and front views (tools/trace/a319/), starting from the A320's points moved by the shorter fuselage; the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. Both sheets are drawn 2.5% short lengthwise and are evened out to their printed figures. The cabin windows are the drawing's; the cockpit panes the A320's. Many A319s fly without sharklets (wingtip fences): this shape has sharklets.
